For if giving to those who have come in that manner were an offering of flowers, it would not be allowable for novices to give either. ‘By themselves’ means the novices by themselves. ‘Taking rice-gruel, food, etc.’—this is said with reference to the procuring of rice-gruel, food, and other things for the bhikkhus; therefore, it is said without distinction, ‘it is not proper.’

Vuttanayenevāti mātāpitūnaṃ tāva haritvāpi harāpetvāpi pakkositvāpi pakkosāpetvāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭati, sesañātakānaṃ pakkosāpetvāva. Mātāpitūnañca harāpentena ñātisāmaṇereheva harāpetabbaṃ, itare pana yadi sayameva icchanti, vaṭṭatīti imaṃ pupphe vuttanayaṃ phalepi [M 2.0377] atidisati, tasmā phalampi mātāpitūnaṃ haraṇaharāpanādinā dātuṃ vaṭṭati, sesañātīnaṃ pakkosāpetvāva. Idāni “yo haritvā vā harāpetvā vā…pe… issaravatāya dadato thullaccaya”nti imaṃ pupphe vuttanayaṃ phalepi saṅkhipitvā dassento “kulasaṅgahatthāya panā”tiādimāha. Khīṇaparibbayānanti āgantuke sandhāya vuttaṃ. Phalaparicchedena vāti “ettakāni phalāni dātabbānī”ti evaṃ phalaparicchedena vā. Rukkhaparicchedena vāti “imehi rukkhehi dātabbānī”ti evaṃ rukkhaparicchedena vā. Paricchinnesupi rukkhesu “idha phalāni sundarāni, ito gaṇhathā”ti vadantena kulasaṅgaho kato nāma hotīti āha “evaṃ pana na vattabba”nti.

‘By the stated method’ means, first, for parents, it is allowable to give by bringing, having brought, summoning, or having summoned them. For other relatives, only by having them summoned. And when having things brought for parents, it should be done only by novice relatives; as for other novices, if they themselves wish to do so, it is allowable. He extends this method stated regarding flowers to fruits as well. Therefore, fruits too may be given to parents by means of bringing, having them brought, and so on, but for other relatives, only by having them summoned. Now, by summarizing and showing that this method stated regarding flowers—‘Whoever, by bringing or having brought… (etc.) … for one who gives with the manner of an authority, there is a grave offense’—applies to fruits as well, he says, ‘But for the sake of supporting a family,’ etc. ‘Of those whose provisions are exhausted’ is said with reference to guests. ‘By specifying the fruits’ means by specifying the fruits thus: ‘This many fruits should be given.’ ‘By specifying the trees’ means by specifying the trees thus: ‘Fruits from these trees should be given.’ Even when trees are specified, if one says, ‘The fruits here are beautiful, take from here,’ it is considered that supporting a family has been done. Therefore, he says, ‘But one should not speak thus.’

Rukkhacchallīti rukkhattaco. Tesaṃ tesaṃ gihīnaṃ gāmantaradesantarādīsu sāsanapaṭisāsanaharaṇaṃ jaṅghapesanikaṃ. Tenāha “gihīnaṃ dūteyyaṃ sāsanaharaṇakamma”nti. Dūtassa kammaṃ dūteyyaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ sāsanaṃ aggahetvāpi…pe… pade pade dukkaṭanti idaṃ tassa sāsanaṃ ārocessāmīti iminā adhippāyena gamanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tassa pana sāsanaṃ paṭikkhipitvā sayameva kāruññe ṭhito gantvā attano patirūpaṃ sāsanaṃ āroceti, anāpatti. Pubbe vuttappakāranti “mama vacanena bhagavato pāde vandathā”tiādinā vuttappakāraṃ sikkhāpade paṭhamaṃ vuttaṃ. Pakkamatāyasmāti idaṃ pabbājanīyakammavasena vuttaṃ. Puna pakkamatāyasmāti idaṃ pana pabbājanīyakammakatassa vattavasena vuttaṃ. Paṭhamasaṅghabhedasadisānevāti ettha aṅgesupi yathā tattha parakkamanaṃ, evaṃ idha chandādīhi pāpanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sesaṃ tādisamevāti.

‘Tree-bark’ means tree-skin. For various householders, carrying messages and counter-messages to other villages, other regions, and so forth is the work of a foot-messenger. Therefore, it is said, ‘For householders, messengership is the work of carrying messages.’ The work of a messenger is messengership. ‘Even without first accepting the message… (etc.) … at every step there is a dukkaṭa offense’—this is said with reference to going with the intention, ‘I will deliver his message.’ However, if one rejects his message and, standing in compassion, goes and delivers a message suitable to oneself, there is no offense. ‘The previously stated manner’ refers to the manner first stated in the training rule, such as ‘By my word, pay homage to the Blessed One’s feet.’ ‘Depart, venerable sir’—this is said in connection with the act of expulsion. Again, ‘Depart, venerable sir’—this is said with reference to the proper conduct for one who has been subjected to the act of expulsion. ‘It is similar to the first Saṅghādisesa’—here, it should be understood that just as there was exertion in the factors of that rule, so here there is the bringing about by means of desire and so forth. The rest is just the same.

Kuladūsakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the corrupter of families is concluded.

Nigamanavaṇṇanā

The commentary on the Conclusion.

442. Paṭhamaṃ [V 2.0334] āpatti āpajjanaṃ etesanti paṭhamāpattikā. Tattakāni ahānīti paṭicchāditadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva ārocitadivaso, tāva divasapakkhamāsasaṃvaccharavasena yattako kālo atikkanto, tattakaṃ kālanti attho. Akāmena avasenāti ettha appaṭikammakatāya āpattiyā saggamokkhāvaraṇabhāvato anicchantenapi parivasitabbanti [M 2.0378] adhippāyo. Avhātabboti abbhānakammavasena pakkositabbo. Te ca bhikkhū gārayhāti ettha ye ūnabhāvaṃ ñatvā abbhenti, te bhikkhū ca garahitabbā sātisārā sadosā, dukkaṭaṃ āpajjantīti ayamattho pākaṭoyevāti na vutto. Sāmīcīti vattaṃ.

442. They are called 'paṭhamāpattikā' because for them there is the first incurring of an offense. 'That much time' means: from the day of concealment up to the day of declaration, whatever time has elapsed in terms of days, fortnights, months, or years—that much time is the meaning. Here, 'unwillingly and without control' means that even if one does not wish to, one must undergo parivāsa, because the unatoned offense obstructs heaven and liberation; this is the intention. 'Should be summoned' means he should be called by means of the act of rehabilitation (abbhāna). Here, 'and those bhikkhus are blameworthy' means that those bhikkhus who, knowing the deficiency, grant rehabilitation—those bhikkhus are also blameworthy, having transgression and fault, and they incur a dukkaṭa offense. This meaning is quite clear, therefore it is not stated. 'Sāmīcī' means proper conduct.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya sāratthadīpaniyaṃ

Thus, in the Sāratthadīpanī, a sub-commentary to the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya—

Terasakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the section of thirteen is concluded.

3. Aniyatakaṇḍaṃ

3. The Chapter on the Undetermined

1. Paṭhamaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Indeterminate Training Rule

443. Puttasaddena [V 2.0335][M 2.0379] sāmaññaniddesato ekasesanayena vā puttīpi gahitāti āha “bahū dhītaro cā”ti. Dānappadānesūti khuddakesu ceva mahantesu ca dānesu. Chaṇaṃ nāma attano gehe kattabbamaṅgalanti āha “āvāhavivāhamaṅgalādīsū”ti. Ettha ādi-saddena phagguṇamāsādīsu uttaraphagguṇādiabhilakkhitadivasesu saparijanānaṃ manussānaṃ maṅgalakaraṇampi saṅgaṇhāti. Antarussavesūti mahussavassa antarantarā pavattitaussavesu. Āsāḷhīpavāraṇanakkhattādīsūti ettha nakkhattasaddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Tattha āsāḷhīnakkhattanti vassūpagamanapūjādivasaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, pavāraṇanakkhattanti pavāraṇapūjādivasaṃ sandhāya. Ādi-saddena yasmiṃ nakkhatte gāmanigamavāsino tayo satta vā divase nakkhattaghosanaṃ katvā yathāvibhavaṃ alaṅkatapaṭiyattā bhoge paribhuñjantā nakkhattakīḷaṃ kīḷanti, tampi saṅgaṇhāti. Imepi dārakāti attano dārake sandhāya vadanti. Tadanantaranti bhikkhūnaṃ bhojanānantaraṃ.

3. By the term 'putta' (son), daughters are also included through general reference or by way of the ekasesa method, hence it is said, 'and many daughters.' 'In gifts and offerings' means in both small and large gifts. The term 'chaṇa' refers to an auspicious ceremony to be performed in one's own home, hence it is said, 'in weddings, marriage celebrations, and other auspicious ceremonies.' Here, the term 'etc.' also includes auspicious ceremonies performed by people with their families on days marked by asterisms such as Uttaraphagguṇī in months such as Phagguṇa. 'In intermittent festivals' means in festivals that occur in the intervals between major festivals. Regarding 'in the Āsāḷhī and Pavāraṇā festivals, etc.,' here the term 'festival' (nakkhatta) should be applied to each individually. Therein, the 'Āsāḷhī festival' is said with reference to the day of observance for entering the rains-residence, and the 'Pavāraṇā festival' is said with reference to the day of the Pavāraṇā observance. The term 'etc.' also includes occasions when villagers and town-dwellers, after announcing a festival for three or seven days, enjoy their wealth, adorned and prepared according to their means, while engaging in festival play. 'These too are children' is said with reference to their own children. 'Immediately after that' means immediately after the bhikkhus' meal.

444-445. Taṃ kammanti taṃ ajjhācārakammaṃ. Bhikkhu nisinneti ettha bhikkhūti bhummatthe paccattavacanaṃ, bhummavacanassa vā lopaṃ katvā niddesoti āha “bhikkhumhi nisinne”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ “sotassa raho”ti idaṃ atthuddhāravasena vuttaṃ, “paṭicchanne āsane”ti pana vacanato “sakkā hoti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitu”nti ca vuttattā cakkhussa raho idhādhippetoti dassetuṃ “kiñcāpī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Paricchedo veditabboti raho nisajjāpattiyā paricchedo vavatthānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Idāni cakkhussa raheneva āpattiṃ paricchinditvā dassento “sacepi hī”tiādimāha. Pihitakavāṭassāti iminā paṭicchannabhāvato cakkhussa rahosabbhāvaṃ dasseti. Apihitakavāṭassāti iminā appaṭicchannabhāvaṃ dasseti. Appaṭicchanne ca dutiyasikkhāpade āgatanayena sotassa rahavasenapi paricchedo veditabboti āha “antodvādasahatthepi okāse”ti[V 2.0336]. “Antodvādasahatthe”ti hi idaṃ sotassa rahābhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yadi hi cakkhusseva rahābhāvaṃ sandhāya vadeyya[M 2.0380], “antodvādasahatthe”ti na vadeyya appaṭicchanne tato dūratare nisinnepi cakkhussa rahāsambhavato. Yasmā nisīditvā niddāyanto kapimiddhapareto kañci kālaṃ cakkhūni ummīleti, kañci kālaṃ nimīleti, na ca mahāniddaṃ okkamati, tasmā “niddāyantopi anāpattiṃ karotī”ti vuttaṃ. Nipajjitvā niddāyanto pana tādiso na hotīti āha “nipajjitvā niddāyanto na karotī”ti, anāpattiṃ na karotīti attho.

1. That deed means that transgressive deed. 'A bhikkhu sitting': here, the word 'bhikkhu' is a nominative used in the sense of the locative, or it is a statement made with the elision of the locative ending, hence it is said, 'when a bhikkhu is sitting.' In the Pāḷi, 'secluded to the ear' is stated by way of extracting the meaning, but since it is said 'in a concealed seat' and 'it is possible to engage in sexual intercourse,' the passage beginning 'kiñcāpi' (even though) is stated to indicate that seclusion to the eye is intended here. 'The delimitation should be understood' means the delimitation and determination of the offense of sitting in seclusion should be understood. Now, showing the delimitation of the offense by seclusion to the eye alone, he states the passage beginning 'sacepi hi' (even if). By 'with the door closed,' he shows the existence of seclusion to the eye due to its concealed nature. By 'with the door open,' he shows the absence of concealment. And in an unconcealed place, the delimitation should be understood also in terms of seclusion to the ear, according to the method given in the second training rule. Hence it is said, 'even within a space of twelve cubits.' For the phrase 'within twelve cubits' is stated with reference to the absence of seclusion to the ear. If it were stated with reference only to the absence of seclusion to the eye, it would not say 'within twelve cubits,' because of the impossibility of seclusion to the eye even when sitting further away in an unconcealed place. Since one who sits and dozes, overcome by monkey-like drowsiness, sometimes opens and sometimes closes his eyes, and does not fall into deep sleep, it is said, 'even one who is dozing brings about non-offense.' However, one who lies down and sleeps is not like that—hence it is said, 'one who lies down and sleeps does not,' meaning he does not bring about non-offense.

Paṭiladdhasotāpattiphalāti antimaparicchedato ariyasāvikaṃ dasseti. Paṭividdhacatusaccāti sotāpattimaggena paṭividdhacatusaccā. Tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarena kāretabboti nisajjaṃ paṭijānamānassa tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarasamāyogo hotiyevāti vuttaṃ. Pārājikena pana saṅghādisesena ca pācittiyena ca tenākārena nisajjaṃ paṭijānamānova kāretabbo. Na appaṭijānamānoti alajjīpi appaṭijānamāno āpattiyā na kāretabboti avisesena vuttaṃ. So hi yāva na paṭijānāti, tāva neva suddho, na asuddhoti vā vattabbo, vattānusandhinā pana kāretabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ –

443. 'She who has attained the fruit of stream-entry' shows a noble female disciple by way of the final determination. 'Having penetrated the four truths' means having penetrated the four truths through the path of stream-entry. 'To be dealt with for one of three offenses' means it is said that for one who admits to sitting down, there is inevitably an association with one of these three offenses. But one should be dealt with only if one admits to sitting down in such a way as to incur a pārājika, saṅghādisesa, or pācittiya. 'Not if not admitting': this is stated without distinction, meaning that even a shameless one who does not admit should not be dealt with for the offense. For as long as he does not admit, he should be spoken of as neither pure nor impure, but he should be dealt with in accordance with the sequence of the case. And this was said:

“Paṭiññā lajjīsu katā, alajjīsu evaṃ na vijjati;

Bahumpi alajjī bhāseyya, vattānusandhitena kāraye”ti. (pari. 359);

"A confession is made among the modest; such is not found among the shameless. Though a shameless person may say much, one should deal with him in accordance with the sequence of the case."

Yena vā sā saddheyyavacasā upāsikā vadeyya, tena so bhikkhu kāretabboti ettha “paṭijānamāno”ti avuttepi adhikārattā “paṭijānamānova tena so bhikkhu kāretabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Tathārūpāya upāsikāya vacanena aññathattābhāvato diṭṭhaṃ nāma tathāpi hoti, aññathāpi hotīti dassanena aññathattasambhavaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ mahiddhikā nāma…pe… vadāpethāti idaṃ “evaṃ mahiddhikāpi tumhe evarūpe āsaṅkanīye ṭhāne kasmā anupaparikkhitvā nisinnattha, tumhādisehi nāma antaraghare nisīdantehi upaparikkhitvā patirūpe ṭhāne nisīditabba”nti theraṃ ovadanto āha, na pana asaddahanto. Thero attano anupaparikkhitvā anisinnabhāvaṃ dassento “antaragharasseveso āvuso doso”ti āha. Evamakāsinti attano nigūhitabbampi guṇaṃ pakāsento evaṃ [M 2.0381] viya iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ akāsiṃ. Rakkheyyāsi manti “mā maṃ aññepi evaṃ jānantū”ti attano guṇaṃ ajānāpetukāmo vadati.

Whatever a laywoman whose word is trustworthy might say, the bhikkhu should be dealt with according to that. Here, even though 'confessing' is not stated, because it is the governing principle, it is said, 'That bhikkhu should be dealt with only if he confesses.' Because there is no discrepancy in the words of such a laywoman, he demonstrates the possibility of discrepancy in what is seen by showing that 'what is seen can indeed be so, and it can also be otherwise.' As for the phrase 'Thus, those of great psychic power... you should make them speak,' this was said by one admonishing the elder, not out of disbelief: 'Even you, who possess such great psychic power, why did you sit in such a suspicious place without investigating? Those like you, when sitting inside a house, ought to investigate and sit in a suitable place.' The elder, wishing to show that he had not sat down without first investigating, said, 'Friend, this is simply the fault of being inside a house.' As for 'I acted thus,' it means: 'Revealing even a quality that ought to have been concealed, I performed a miracle of psychic power like this.' As for 'You should protect me,' he says this wishing not to let his virtue be known to others, meaning, 'Let others not know of me in this way.'

446-451. Mātugāmassa methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantoti ettha “magge”ti pāṭhaseso daṭṭhabboti [V 2.0337] āha “mātugāmassa magge”ti. Raho nisajjassādassa asatipi methunarāgabhāve tappaṭibaddhakilesattā vuttaṃ “methunadhammasannissitakileso vuccatī”ti, teneva sannissitaggahaṇaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ sandhāya agatepi asuddhacittena gatattā “assāde uppanne pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ. Rahassādo uppajjati anāpattīti suddhacittena gantvā nisinnattā cittuppādamattenettha āpatti na hotīti vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ dhammo aniyatoti ettha tiṇṇaṃ āpattīnaṃ yaṃ āpattiṃ vā vatthuṃ vā paṭijānāti, tassa vasena kāretabbatāya aniyatoti ayamattho pākaṭoyevāti na vutto. Yaṃ āpattiṃ paṭijānāti, tassā vasenettha aṅgabhedo veditabbo.

Regarding 'engaging in sexual intercourse with a woman,' here the remainder of the reading, 'in the path,' should be understood; thus, he said, 'in a woman's path (vagina).' For one who delights in sitting in seclusion, even if there is no state of sexual lust, because it is a defilement connected to it, it is said, 'it is called a defilement associated with sexual intercourse'; for that reason, the word 'associated' is used. With reference to that, even when one has come, because of having gone with an impure mind, it is said, 'when pleasure arises, it is a pācittiya offense.' As for the statement 'If pleasure in seclusion arises, it is not an offense,' this is said because, having gone and sat down with a pure mind, an offense does not occur here merely by the arising of a thought. Regarding 'This rule is indeterminate,' here the meaning—that it is indeterminate because one is to be dealt with according to whichever of the three offenses or cases one confesses to—is very clear and therefore not stated. The division of components here should be understood according to whichever offense one confesses to.

Paṭhamaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the First Indeterminate Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Second Indeterminate Training Rule

452. “Eko”ti vuttattā “nisajjaṃ kappetuṃ paṭikkhitta”nti iminā sambandho na ghaṭatīti āha “yaṃ eko…pe… sambandho veditabbo”ti. Etaṃ paccattavacananti “eko”ti idaṃ paccattavacanaṃ.

452. Because 'one' is stated, the connection with 'to arrange a sitting is prohibited' does not fit; thus, he said: 'That which is one... the connection should be understood.' As for 'This is a statement in the singular,' the word 'one' is a statement in the singular.

453. Bahi parikkhittanti bahi pākārādinā parikkhittaṃ. Pariveṇaṅgaṇanti pariveṇamāḷakaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Itthīpi purisopīti ettha paṭhame kasmā itthisatampi anāpattiṃ na karoti, idha ekāpi kasmā anāpattiṃ karotīti? Vuccate – paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ “sakkā hoti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitu”nti vuttattā methunadhammavasena āgataṃ, na ca methunassa mātugāmo dutiyo hoti. Itthiyo hi aññamaññissā vajjaṃ paṭicchādenti, teneva vesāliyaṃ mahāvane dvāraṃ vivaritvā nipanne bhikkhumhi sambahulā itthiyo yāvadatthaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu, tasmā tattha “itthisatampi anāpattiṃ na karotī”ti vuttaṃ. Idaṃ pana sikkhāpadaṃ duṭṭhullavācāvasena āgataṃ “alañca kho hoti mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsitu”nti [M 2.0382] vuttattā. Duṭṭhullavācañca sutvā mātugāmopi na paṭicchādeti. Teneva duṭṭhullavācāsikkhāpade yā tā itthiyo hirimanā, tā nikkhamitvā bhikkhū ujjhāpesuṃ, tasmā idha “itthīpi anāpattiṃ karotī”ti vuttaṃ. Idha appaṭicchannattā itthīpi anāpattiṃ karoti, tattha paṭicchannattā itthisatampi anāpattiṃ na karotīti ca vadanti.

453. `Enclosed outside` means enclosed outside by a wall and the like. `Pariveṇaṅgaṇa` (monastery grounds) is said with reference to the monastery's upper terrace. Regarding 'a woman also, a man also,' here a question is raised: In the first [Aniyata rule], why does the presence of even a hundred women not lead to a verdict of 'no offense,' whereas here, the presence of even one woman does lead to a verdict of 'no offense'? It is said: The first training rule comes by way of sexual intercourse, as it is stated, 'it is possible to engage in sexual intercourse.' And a woman is not a reliable second person regarding sexual intercourse. For women conceal one another's faults. For that very reason, in the Great Forest at Vesālī, when a monk was lying down after opening the door, many women did as they pleased and then departed. Therefore, in that case, it was said, 'the presence of even a hundred women does not lead to a verdict of "no offense".' This training rule, however, comes by way of lewd speech, as it is stated, 'it is sufficient to address a woman with lewd speech.' And a woman, upon hearing lewd speech, does not conceal it. For that very reason, in the training rule concerning lewd speech, those women who were modest went out and caused the monks to be criticized. Therefore, here it is said, 'the presence of even one woman leads to a verdict of "no offense".' They also say: Here, because it is not concealed, the presence of even one woman leads to a verdict of 'no offense'; there, because it is concealed, the presence of even a hundred women does not lead to a verdict of 'no offense'.

Kāyasaṃsaggavasena anandho vutto, duṭṭhullavācāvasena abadhiro. Antodvādasahatthe okāseti sotassa rahābhāvo vutto, etena “sotassa raho dvādasahatthena paricchinditabbo”ti dasseti[V 2.0338]. Tasmā dvādasahatthato bahi nisinno anāpattiṃ na karoti satipi cakkhussa rahābhāve sotassa rahasabbhāvato. Imasmiñhi sikkhāpade appaṭicchannattā sotassa rahoyeva adhippeto. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “cakkhussa raho”ti atthuddhāravasena vuttaṃ. Kenaci pana “dvepi rahā idha adhippetā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Na hi appaṭicchanne okāse cakkhussa raho sambhavati dvādasahatthato bahi dassanavisaye dūratare nisinnassapi daṭṭhuṃ sakkuṇeyyabhāvato. Niddāyantopīti iminā “nipajjitvā niddāyantopi gahitoyevā”ti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. “Nipajjitvā niddāyantepi satipi cakkhussa rahe abadhirattā sotassa raho natthī”ti gaṇṭhipadakārānaṃ adhippāyo. Yathā pana nipajjitvā niddāyanto andho viya kiñci na passatīti cakkhussa raho sambhavati, tathā badhiro viya kiñci saddaṃ na suṇātīti sotassa rahopi sambhavatīti sakkā vattuṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyañca ṭhito vā nisinno vāti ettakameva vuttaṃ, paṭhamasikkhāpade viya “nipajjitvā niddāyantopi anāpattiṃ na karotī”ti idaṃ pana na vuttaṃ, tasmā vīmaṃsitvā yathā na virujjhati, tathā gahetabbaṃ.

With regard to physical contact, one is said to be 'not blind'; with regard to lewd speech, 'not deaf.' In the phrase 'in a space within twelve cubits,' the absence of privacy for the ear is stated. By this, it shows that 'the privacy for the ear is to be determined by twelve cubits.' Therefore, one sitting beyond twelve cubits does not commit an offense, for even if there is an absence of privacy for the eye, there is the existence of privacy for the ear. Indeed, in this training rule, because it is an unconcealed place, only privacy for the ear is intended. In the Pāḷi, however, 'privacy for the eye' is stated by way of extracting a meaning. But it has been said by some that 'both types of privacy are intended here'; that should not be accepted. For in an unconcealed space, privacy for the eye is not possible, because even one sitting further away, beyond twelve cubits but within the range of vision, can be seen. By the phrase 'even one who is sleeping,' it is stated in all three Ganthipada texts that 'one who is lying down and sleeping is also included.' The opinion of the Ganthipada authors is: 'For one who is lying down and sleeping, even though there is privacy for the eye, because they are not deaf, there is no privacy for the ear.' However, it can be argued that just as one lying down and sleeping does not see anything, like a blind person, so there can be privacy for the eye; similarly, as they do not hear any sound, like a deaf person, so there can also be privacy for the ear. And in the Commentary, only 'standing or sitting' is stated; unlike in the first training rule, the statement 'for one lying down and sleeping there is no offense' is not made here. Therefore, having investigated the matter, it should be understood in such a way that there is no contradiction.

Sotassa rahasseva idhādhippetattā “badhiro pana cakkhumāpī”ti vuttaṃ. Andhassa appaṭicchannampi paṭicchannapakkhaṃ bhajatīti paṭhamasikkhāpadassa visayattā vuttaṃ “andho vā abadhiropi na karotī”ti. Yatheva hi tattha apihitakavāṭassa gabbhassa anto samīpepi ṭhito andho anāpattiṃ na karoti, evamayampīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ubhayatthāpīti dvīsupi aniyatesu. Yasmā dvīhi sikkhāpadehi udāyittheraṃ ārabbha visuṃ paññattā kāci āpatti nāma natthi, tasmā tassa tassa sikkhāpadassa ādikammike sandhāya ādikammikānaṃ anāpatti vuttā. Upanandattherādayo hi raho nisajjādīnaṃ [M 2.0383] ādikammikā. Bhagavatā pana paṭhamaṃ paññattasikkhāpadāniyeva gahetvā upanandavatthusmiṃ aniyatakkamo dassito. Yadi imehi sikkhāpadehi visuṃ paññattā āpatti nāma natthi, atha kasmā bhagavatā aniyatadvayaṃ paññattanti? Evarūpāyapi upāsikāya vuccamāno paṭijānamānoyeva āpattiyā kāretabbo, na appaṭijānamānoti dassentena bhagavatā yāya kāyaci āpattiyā yena kenaci codite paṭiññātakaraṇaṃyeva daḷhaṃ katvā vinayavinicchayalakkhaṇaṃ ṭhapitaṃ. Atha bhikkhunīnaṃ aniyataṃ kasmā na vuttanti? Idameva lakkhaṇaṃ sabbattha anugatanti na vuttaṃ.

Because only the privacy of the ear is intended here, it is said, 'But a deaf person, even if sighted.' Since for a blind person, even what is unconcealed is treated as concealed, and because it is the domain of the first training rule, it is said, 'A blind person or one who is not deaf does not do it.' Just as there, a blind person standing even near the inside of a room with an unclosed door does not commit an offense, so too should this be understood. `In both cases` refers to the two indefinite rules. Since there is no offense whatsoever designated separately by these two training rules concerning the Elder Udāyi, therefore, with reference to the initial offenders of each training rule, it is stated that there is no offense for the initial offenders. Indeed, the Elder Upananda and others were the initial offenders regarding private sitting and so on. However, the Blessed One, having taken only the training rules that were laid down first, showed the sequence of the indefinite rules in the case of Upananda. If there is no offense designated separately by these two training rules, then why did the Blessed One establish the two indefinite rules? The Blessed One, by showing that even when addressed by such a female lay follower, one who admits it should be dealt with for the offense, and one who does not admit it should not, firmly established the act of admission itself as the defining characteristic of disciplinary judgment when accused by anyone of any offense whatsoever. Then why was an indefinite rule not stated for bhikkhunīs? It was not stated because this very characteristic is applicable everywhere.

Dutiyaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Second Indefinite Training Rule is concluded.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya sāratthadīpaniyaṃ

Thus, in the Sāratthadīpanī, the Subcommentary to the Samantapāsādikā, the Vinaya Commentary—

Aniyatavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Indefinite Rules is concluded.

4. Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

4. The Chapter on Forfeiture

1. Cīvaravaggo

1. The Chapter on Robes

1. Paṭhamakathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Kathina Training Rule

459. Samitāvināti [V 2.0339][M 2.0384] samitapāpena. Gotamake cetiyeti gotamayakkhassa cetiyaṭṭhāne katavihāro vuccati. Paribhuñjituṃ anuññātaṃ hotīti bhagavatā gahapaticīvare anuññāte bahūni cīvarāni labhitvā bhaṇḍikaṃ katvā sīsepi khandhepi kaṭiyāpi ṭhapetvā āgacchante bhikkhū disvā cīvare sīmaṃ bandhantena ticīvaraṃ paribhogatthāya anuññātaṃ, na pana adhiṭṭhānavasena. Nahāyanti etthāti nahānaṃ, nahānatitthaṃ.

459. `Samitāvin` means one with appeased evil. `Gotamake cetiye` refers to a dwelling said to be built at the shrine site of the Gotama yaksha. `Paribhuñjituṃ anuññātaṃ hoti` means that when the Blessed One permitted robes from householders, monks, having obtained many robes and made them into bundles, were seen coming carrying them on their heads, shoulders, and waists. Seeing this, the Blessed One, by establishing a boundary for robes, permitted the triple robe for use, but not by way of determination. `Nahāyanti ettha` ('They bathe here'), hence `nahānaṃ` ('a bathing place'); a bathing ford.

460. Eko kira brāhmaṇo cintesi “buddharatanassa ca saṅgharatanassa ca pūjā paññāyati, kathaṃ nu kho dhammaratanaṃ pūjitaṃ nāma hotī”ti. So bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchi. Bhagavā āha “sacepi brāhmaṇa dhammaratanaṃ pūjetukāmo, ekaṃ bahussutaṃ pūjehī”ti. Bahussutaṃ bhante ācikkhathāti. Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pucchāti. So bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā “bahussutaṃ bhante ācikkhathā”ti āha. Ānandatthero brāhmaṇāti. Brāhmaṇo theraṃ sahassagghanakena cīvarena pūjesi. Tena vuttaṃ “paṭilābhavasena uppanna”nti. Uppanna-saddo nipphannapariyāyopi hotīti taṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “no nipphattivasenā”ti. Paṭhamameva hi taṃ tantavāyakammena nipphannaṃ.

460. A certain brahmin, it is said, thought, 'Offerings to the Buddha jewel and the Saṅgha jewel are evident, but how indeed is the Dhamma jewel honored?' He approached the Blessed One and asked this matter. The Blessed One said, 'Brahmin, if you wish to honor the Dhamma jewel, honor one who is very learned.' 'Venerable sir, indicate one who is very learned,' he asked. 'Ask the community of monks,' He said. He approached the monks and said, 'Venerable sirs, indicate one who is very learned.' They replied, 'Brahmin, the Elder Ānanda is very learned.' The brahmin honored the elder with a robe worth a thousand. Hence it is said, 'arisen due to gain.' The word 'arisen' can also be a synonym for 'produced,' so rejecting that, it is said, 'not in the sense of being produced.' For it was produced from the very beginning by the work of the weaver.

Therassa santike upajjhaṃ gāhāpetvā sayaṃ anussāvanakammaṃ karotīti ettha sāriputtattheropi tatheva karotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ ekamekena attano pattacīvaraṃ datvā pabbājetvā upajjhaṃ gaṇhāpitāni [V 2.0340] pañca pañca bhikkhusatāni ahesuṃ. Āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ ativiya mamāyatīti ānandatthero tāva mamāyatu akhīṇāsavabhāvato, sāriputtatthero kathanti? Na idaṃ mamāyanaṃ gehassitapemavasena, atha kho guṇasambhāvanāvasenāti nāyaṃ doso. Navamaṃ vā divasaṃ dasamaṃ vāti bhummatthe upayogavacanaṃ[M 2.0385], navame vā dasame vā divaseti attho. Sace bhaveyyāti sace kassaci evaṃ siyā. Vuttasadisamevāti ettha “vuttadivasamevā”tipi paṭhanti. Dhāretunti ettha “āhā”ti pāṭhaseso daṭṭhabbo.

Regarding 'Having had them take a preceptor in the presence of the elder, he himself performs the act of announcement,' here it should be understood that the Elder Sāriputta also did the same. In this way, for each of them, by giving his own bowl and robe, there were five hundred monks ordained and given a preceptor. Regarding 'he cherished the Venerable Ānanda exceedingly': let the Elder Ānanda be cherished, due to his state of not yet being one whose cankers are destroyed; but how could the Elder Sāriputta be? This cherishing is not by way of affection based on the household life, but rather by way of esteem for his virtues, so there is no fault. Regarding `navamaṃ vā divasaṃ dasamaṃ vā`, this is an accusative used in the sense of the locative; the meaning is 'on the ninth or tenth day'. `Sace bhaveyya` means: if it should be so for someone. Regarding `vuttasadisameva`, here some also read `vuttadivasameva`. Regarding `dhārentu`, the remainder of the text, `āha`, should be understood.

462-463. Niṭṭhitacīvarasminti bhummavacanassa lopaṃ katvā niddesoti āha “niṭṭhite cīvarasmi”nti, cīvarassa karaṇapalibodhe upacchinneti vuttaṃ hoti. Pāsapaṭṭagaṇṭhikapaṭṭapariyosānaṃ yaṃ kiñci kātabbaṃ, taṃ katvāti yojetabbaṃ. Sūciyā paṭisāmananti idaṃ sūcikammassa sammā pariniṭṭhitabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, sūcikammaniṭṭhānamevettha pamāṇaṃ. Etesampīti vinaṭṭhādiṃ parāmasati.

Regarding `Niṭṭhitacīvarasmin`: this is a directive made by eliding the locative ending; therefore, he says, `niṭṭhite cīvarasmin` ('when the robe is finished'). This means that the impediment of making the robe has been cut off. It should be construed as: 'having done whatever needs to be done, up to and including the border-strip and the binding-strip'. The phrase `sūciyā paṭisāmanaṃ` ('putting away the needle') is stated to show the proper completion of the needlework; here, the completion of the needlework is itself the measure. By `etesaṃpi` ('even of these'), he refers to 'the lost', and so on.

Kathine ca ubbhatasminti yaṃ saṅghassa kathinaṃ atthataṃ, tasmiṃ kathine ca ubbhateti attho. Dutiyassa palibodhassa abhāvaṃ dassetīti āvāsapalibodhassa abhāvaṃ dasseti. Ettha ca “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti imehi dvīhi padehi dvinnaṃ palibodhānaṃ abhāvadassanena atthatakathinassa pañcamāsabbhantare yāva cīvarapalibodho āvāsapalibodho ca na upacchijjati, tāva anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappitaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dasāhato parampi ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Atthatakathinassa hi yāva kathinassa ubbhārā anāmantacāro asamādānacāro yāvadatthacīvaraṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ yo ca tattha cīvaruppādoti ime pañcānisaṃsā labbhanti. Pakkamanaṃ anto assāti pakkamanantikā. Evaṃ sesāpi veditabbā. Vitthāro panettha āgataṭṭhāneyeva āvi bhavissati.

“When the Kathina is removed” means: when that Kathina which was spread for the Saṅgha is removed. “It shows the absence of the second impediment” means it shows the absence of the dwelling impediment. And here, by these two phrases, “when the robes are finished” and “when the Kathina is removed,” by showing the absence of the two impediments, it is shown that for a bhikkhu whose Kathina has been spread, within the five-month period, for as long as the robe-impediment and the dwelling-impediment are not cut off, it is permissible to keep an extra robe that is not determined and not formally shared for even longer than ten days. Indeed, for a bhikkhu whose Kathina has been spread, until the Kathina is removed, these five benefits are obtained: wandering without asking permission, wandering without the set of three robes, possessing as many robes as desired, group meals, and whatever robe-arisings there are there. Because departure is its end, it is called `pakkamanantikā`. Thus the remaining terms should also be understood. The detailed explanation of this will become clear in the place where it appears.

Khomanti khomasuttehi vāyitaṃ khomapaṭacīvaraṃ, tathā sesāni. Sāṇanti sāṇavākasuttehi katacīvaraṃ. Bhaṅganti khomasuttādīni sabbāni ekaccāni vā missetvā katacīvaraṃ. Bhaṅgampi vākamayamevāti keci. Dukūlaṃ paṭṭuṇṇaṃ somārapaṭaṃ cīnapaṭaṃ iddhijaṃ devadinnanti imāni pana cha cīvarāni etesaṃyeva anulomānīti visuṃ na vuttāni. Dukūlañhi sāṇassa anulomaṃ vākamayattā. Paṭṭuṇṇadese sañjātavatthaṃ paṭṭuṇṇaṃ. “Paṭṭuṇṇakoseyyaviseso”ti hi abhidhānakose vuttaṃ. Somāradese cīnadese ca jātavatthāni somāracīnapaṭāni. Paṭṭuṇṇādīni tīṇi koseyyassa anulomāni pāṇakehi katasuttamayattā. Iddhijaṃ ehibhikkhūnaṃ [M 2.0386] puññiddhiyā nibbattacīvaraṃ, taṃ khomādīnaṃ [V 2.0341] aññataraṃ hotīti tesaṃ eva anulomaṃ. Devatāhi dinnaṃ cīvaraṃ devadinnaṃ, taṃ kapparukkhe nibbattaṃ jāliniyā devakaññāya anuruddhattherassa dinnavatthasadisaṃ, tampi khomādīnaṃyeva anulomaṃ hoti tesu aññatarabhāvato.

`Khoma` means a `khoma`-cloth robe woven from linen threads; likewise for the others. `Sāṇa` means a robe made from hemp-bark threads. `Bhaṅga` means a robe made by mixing all or some of linen threads and so on. Some say that `bhaṅga` is also made of bark fiber. Now, these six robes—`dukūla`, `paṭṭuṇṇa`, `somārapaṭa`, `cīnapaṭa`, `iddhija`, and `devadinna`—are not mentioned separately because they are analogues of these very ones. For `dukūla` is an analogue of hemp because it is made of bark fiber. `Paṭṭuṇṇa` is cloth originating in the Paṭṭuṇṇa country. Indeed, in the Abhidhānakosa it is said: “`Paṭṭuṇṇa` is a special kind of silk (`koseyya`).” `Somārapaṭa` and `cīnapaṭa` are cloths originating in the Somāra and Cīna countries. `Paṭṭuṇṇa` and the other two are analogues of silk because they are made from thread produced by living creatures. `Iddhija` is a robe that arises through the psychic power of merit of the `ehi-bhikkhus`; since it is one of the types such as `khoma`, it is an analogue of them. `Devadinna` is a robe given by devas; it is produced from a celestial wish-fulfilling tree, like the cloth given to the Elder Anuruddha by the deva-maiden Jālinī. That too is an analogue of `khoma` and the others, because it is one of those types.

Majjhimassa purisassa vidatthiṃ sandhāya “dve vidatthiyo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Iminā dīghato vaḍḍhakīhatthappamāṇaṃ vitthārato tato upaḍḍhappamāṇaṃ vikappanupaganti dasseti. Tathā hi “sugatavidatthi nāma idāni majjhimassa purisassa tisso vidatthiyo, vaḍḍhakīhatthena diyaḍḍho hattho hotī”ti kuṭikārasikkhāpadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.348-349) vuttaṃ, tasmā sugataṅgulena dvādasaṅgulaṃ vaḍḍhakīhatthena diyaḍḍho hatthoti siddhaṃ. Evañca katvā sugataṅgulena aṭṭhaṅgulaṃ vaḍḍhakīhatthappamāṇanti idaṃ āgatamevāti.

With reference to the span of a medium-sized man, it is said, “Two spans,” and so on. By this, it is shown that in length, it is the measure of a carpenter's cubit, and in width, half of that measure is suitable for formal sharing. For it is stated in the commentary on the Kuṭikāra training rule: “The Sugata's span is now three spans of a medium-sized man, which equals one and a half cubits by the carpenter's measure.” Therefore, it is established that twelve Sugata finger-widths are one and a half cubits by the carpenter's measure. And this being so, it follows that eight Sugata finger-widths are the measure of a carpenter's cubit.

Taṃ atikkāmayatoti ettha tanti cīvaraṃ kālaṃ vā parāmasati. Tassa yo aruṇoti tassa cīvaruppādadivasassa yo atikkanto aruṇo. Cīvaruppādadivasena saddhinti cīvaruppādadivasassa atikkantaaruṇena saddhinti attho. Divasasaddena hi taṃdivasanissito aruṇo vutto. Bandhitvāti rajjuādīhi bandhitvā. Veṭhetvāti vatthādīti veṭhetvā.

In “He causes it to be passed over,” “it” refers to the robe or the time. “The dawn of that” means the dawn that has passed of that day of the robe-arising. “Together with the day of the robe-arising” means together with the passed dawn of the day of the robe-arising. For by the word 'day', the dawn associated with that day is meant.

Vacanīyoti saṅghaṃ apekkhitvā vuttaṃ. Aññathāpi vattabbanti ettha “yāya kāyaci bhāsāya padapaṭipāṭiyā avatvāpi atthamatte vutte vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Tenāti āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇhantena. Paṭiggāhakena “passasī”ti vutte desakena vattabbavacanaṃ dasseti “āma passāmī”ti. Puna paṭiggāhakena vattabbavacanamāha “āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī”ti. Evaṃ vutte puna desakena vattabbavacanaṃ “sādhu suṭṭhu saṃvarissāmī”ti. Iminā attano āyatiṃ saṃvare patiṭṭhitabhāvaṃ dasseti. Dvīsu pana sambahulāsu vāti dvīsu sambahulāsu vā āpattīsu purimanayeneva vacanabhedo veditabbo. Ñattiyaṃ āpattiṃ sarati vivaratīti ettha dve āpattiyoti vā sambahulā āpattiyoti vā vattabbanti adhippāyo. Cīvaradānepīti nissaṭṭhacīvarassa dānepi. Vatthuvasenāti cīvaragaṇanāya. Gaṇassa vuttā pāḷiyevettha pāḷīti dvīsu imāhaṃ āyasmantānaṃ nissajjāmīti vacane visesābhāvato vuttaṃ. Evaṃ…pe… vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti vatvā tattha kāraṇamāha “ito [M 2.0387] garukatarānī”tiādi. Tattha itoti ito nissaṭṭhacīvaradānato. Ñattikammato ñattidutiyakammaṃ garukataranti āha “ito garukatarānī”ti. Imāhaṃ cīvaranti ettha “imaṃ cīvara”ntipi paṭhanti.

“To be spoken” is said with reference to the Saṅgha. “It may be said otherwise”: here they say, “It is permissible if just the meaning is stated, without uttering the sequence of words in any particular language.” `Tena` (by him) means by the one confessing the offense. When the one receiving the confession says, `Passasi` (Do you see?), it shows the words to be spoken by the confessor: `Āma passāmi` (Yes, I see). Again, he states the words to be spoken by the receiver: `Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsi` (You should restrain yourself in the future). When this is said, the words to be spoken again by the confessor are: `Sādhu suṭṭhu saṃvarissāmi` (Good, I will restrain myself well). By this, he shows that he is established in future restraint. In the case of two or many offenses, the difference in wording should be understood in the same way as before. In the motion (`ñatti`), in the phrase 'recalls and reveals the offense', the intention is that one should say either 'two offenses' or 'many offenses'. `Cīvaradāne pi` means also in the giving of a relinquished robe. `Vatthuvasena` means by the number of robes. The Pāḷi stated for a group is the Pāḷi here; this is said because in the case of two bhikkhus, there is no difference in the wording, `Imāhaṃ āyasmantānaṃ nissajjāmi` (I relinquish these to the venerable sirs). Having said, “Thus... it is permissible to say...”, he states the reason for that: `Ito garukatarāni` (More serious than this), and so on. Therein, `ito` means: from this giving of a relinquished robe. An act consisting of a motion and one announcement (`ñattidutiyakamma`) is more serious than an act consisting of a motion only (`ñattikamma`); therefore he said, `Ito garukatarāni`. In the phrase `imāhaṃ cīvaraṃ` (these robes), some also read `imaṃ cīvaraṃ` (this robe).

468. Na [V 2.0342] idha saññā rakkhatīti idaṃ vematikaṃ anatikkantasaññañca sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yopi evaṃsaññī, tassapīti na kevalaṃ atikkante atikkantasaññissa, atha kho vematikassa anatikkantasaññissapīti attho. “Na idha saññā rakkhatī”tiādinā vuttamatthaṃ sesattikepi atidisati. Esa nayo sabbatthāti esa nayo avinaṭṭhādīsupīti aññesaṃ cīvaresu upacikādīhi khāyitesu “mayhampi cīvaraṃ khāyita”nti evaṃsaññī hotītiādinā yojetabbanti dasseti. Anaṭṭhato aviluttassa visesamāha “pasayhāvahāravasenā”ti. Theyyāvahāravasena gahitañhi naṭṭhanti adhippetaṃ, pasayhāvahāravasena gahitaṃ viluttanti. Anāpatti aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjatīti idaṃ nisīdanasanthataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yaṃ yena hi purāṇasanthatassa sāmantā sugatavidatthiṃ anādiyitvā aññaṃ navaṃ nisīdanasanthataṃ kataṃ, tassa taṃ nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Tasmā “anāpatti aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjatī”ti idaṃ parassa nissaggiyaṃ aparassa paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti imamatthaṃ sādheti. Paribhogaṃ sandhāya vuttanti anatikkante atikkantasaññissa vematikassa ca paribhuñjantasseva dukkaṭaṃ, na pana aparibhuñjitvā ṭhapentassāti adhippāyo.

468. “Perception does not protect here” is said with reference to one who is uncertain and one who perceives it as not having passed beyond. The meaning is that it applies not only to one who perceives it as having passed when it has passed, but indeed also to one who is uncertain and to one who perceives it as not having passed beyond. He extends the meaning stated by “Perception does not protect here,” and so on, to the remaining triads as well. “This is the method everywhere” shows that this method also applies in cases such as “not destroyed,” and so on; when the robes of others are eaten by termites and so on, it should be connected by saying, “he has the perception, ‘My robe has also been eaten,’” and so on. He states the distinction of “not plundered” from “not destroyed” by “by way of forceful taking.” Indeed, what is taken by way of theft is intended as “destroyed,” while what is taken by way of forceful taking is intended as “plundered.” “No offense; having received what was made by another, he uses it” is said with reference to a sitting-rug. For if a new sitting-rug is made by someone without taking a Sugata-span around an old rug, that becomes subject to forfeiture for him. Therefore, “No offense; having received what was made by another, he uses it” establishes this meaning: it is permissible for another to use what is subject to forfeiture for one person. This is said with reference to use; the intention is that for one who perceives it as having passed when it has not passed, and for one who is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct only when using it, but not for one who sets it aside without using it.

469. Ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātunti nāmaṃ vatvā adhiṭṭhātuṃ. Na vikappetunti nāmaṃ vatvā na vikappetuṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Tasmā ticīvarādīni adhiṭṭhahantena “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”tiādinā nāmaṃ vatvā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Vikappentena pana “imaṃ saṅghāṭi”ntiādinā tassa tassa cīvarassa nāmaṃ aggahetvāva “imaṃ cīvaraṃ tuyhaṃ vikappemī”ti vikappetabbaṃ. Ticīvaraṃ vā hotu aññaṃ vā, yadi taṃ taṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā vikappeti, avikappitaṃ hoti, atirekacīvaraṭṭhāneyeva tiṭṭhati. Tato paraṃ vikappetunti “catumāsato paraṃ vikappetvā paribhuñjituṃ anuññāta”nti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Keci pana “tato paraṃ vikappetvā yāva āgāmisaṃvacchare vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ, tāva ṭhapetuṃ anuññāta”ntipi vadanti. “Tato paraṃ vikappetuṃ anujānāmīti ettāvatā vassikasāṭikaṃ kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiñca [M 2.0388] taṃ taṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā vikappetuṃ anuññātanti evamattho na gahetabbo tato paraṃ vassikasāṭikādināmasseva abhāvato. Tasmā tato paraṃ vikappentenapi nāmaṃ gahetvā na vikappetabbaṃ. Ubhinnampi tato paraṃ vikappetvā paribhogassa anuññātattā tathā vikappitaṃ aññanāmena adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjitabba”nti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ.

469. “To determine the triple robe” means to determine it after stating the name. “Not to make an alternative determination” means not to do so after stating the name. This is the method in all cases. Therefore, one determining the triple robe, and so on, should determine it after stating the name, such as, “I determine this outer robe.” But one making an alternative determination should do so without taking the name of each respective robe, such as “this outer robe,” but by saying, “I make this robe an alternative determination for you.” Whether it be the triple robe or another robe, if one makes an alternative determination by taking its specific name, it is not considered to have been made an alternative determination; it remains in the state of an extra robe. “To make an alternative determination beyond that” means “it is permitted to make an alternative determination after four months and use it”—this is stated in all three Gaṇṭhipadas. Some, however, also say, “It is permitted to make an alternative determination beyond that and keep it until the four months of the rains in the coming year.” By the statement, “Beyond that, I allow it to be made an alternative determination,” the meaning that it is permitted to make an alternative determination of the rainy-season cloth and the itch-covering cloth by taking their respective names should not be taken, because beyond that period, the name “rainy-season cloth,” and so on, does not exist. Therefore, even when making an alternative determination beyond that period, one should not do so by taking the name. Since the use of both is permitted after making an alternative determination beyond that period, what has been thus made an alternative determination should be determined under another name and then used”—this is stated in all three Gaṇṭhipadas.

Paccuddharāmīti ṭhapemi, pariccajāmīti vā attho. Imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmīti ettha “imaṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmīti evampi vattuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ, tampi “imaṃ cīvaraṃ parikkhāracoḷaṃ [V 2.0343] adhiṭṭhāmī”ti iminā sameti. Kāyavikāraṃ karontenāti hatthena cīvaraṃ parāmasantena vā cālentena vā. Duvidhanti sammukhaparammukhabhedesu duvidhaṃ. Hatthapāseti idaṃ dvādasahatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tasmā dvādasahatthabbhantare ṭhitaṃ “ima”nti vatvā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Tato paraṃ “eta”nti vatvā adhiṭṭhātabbanti keci vadanti. Gaṇṭhipadesu panettha na kiñci vuttaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhakathāyañca sabbattha “hatthapāso”ti aḍḍhateyyahattho vuccati, tasmā idha visesavikappanāya kāraṇaṃ gavesitabbaṃ. Sāmantavihāro nāma yattha tadaheva gantvā nivattituṃ sakkā. “Sāmantavihāre”ti idaṃ desanāsīsamattaṃ, tasmā ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvā dūre ṭhitampi adhiṭṭhātabbanti vadanti. Ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvāti ca idaṃ ṭhapitaṭṭhānasallakkhaṇaṃ anucchavikanti katvā vuttaṃ, cīvarasallakkhaṇamevettha pamāṇaṃ.

“I rescind” means “I set aside” or “I relinquish.” Regarding “I determine this outer robe,” here it is said in the Gaṇṭhipadas: “It is also permissible to say, ‘I determine this robe as the outer robe,’” and that too accords with “I determine this robe as an accessory cloth.” “By making a bodily gesture” means by touching the robe with the hand or by moving it. “Twofold” means twofold by the division into “in one's presence” and “out of one's presence.” “Within arm’s reach” is said with reference to twelve cubits; therefore, what is within twelve cubits should be determined by saying “this.” Some say that beyond that, it should be determined by saying “that.” Regarding this, nothing is said in the Gaṇṭhipadas. In the Pāḷi and the Commentary, “arm’s reach” is everywhere said to be two and a half cubits; therefore, a reason for this specific interpretation should be sought here. A “neighboring monastery” is one to which one can go and return on that very day. The phrase “in a neighboring monastery” is merely a heading for the teaching; therefore, they say that even what is at a distance may be determined after marking the place where it was put. And the phrase “after marking the place where it was put” is said because marking the place where it was put is suitable; here, the marking of the robe itself is the standard.

Adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitavatthehīti parikkhāracoḷanāmena adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitavatthehi. Adhiṭṭhānato pubbe saṅghāṭiādivohārassa abhāvato “imaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti parikkhāracoḷassa visuṃ paccuddhāravidhiṃ dasseti. Parikkhāracoḷanāmena pana adhiṭṭhitattā “imaṃ parikkhāracoḷaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti vuttepi nevatthi dosoti viññāyati. Paccuddharitvā puna adhiṭṭhātabbānīti idañca saṅghāṭiādicīvaranāmena adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjitukāmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Parikkhāracoḷanāmeneva adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjantassa pana pubbekataadhiṭṭhānameva adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthīti iminā kappabindudānakiccampi natthīti dasseti. Muṭṭhipañcakāditicīvarappamāṇayuttaṃ sandhāya “ticīvaraṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātunti parikkhāracoḷaṃ katvā adhiṭṭhātuṃ. Baddhasīmāyaṃ avippavāsasīmāsammutisabbhāvato cīvaravippavāsepi nevatthi dosoti na tattha dupparihāratāti āha “abaddhasīmāyaṃ dupparihāra”nti.

“By the cloths determined and set aside” means by the cloths determined and set aside with the name “accessory cloth.” Because before the determination there was no usage of terms like “outer robe,” and so on, he shows a separate procedure for rescinding the accessory cloth, saying, “I rescind this.” However, because it has been determined with the name “accessory cloth,” it is understood that even if one says, “I rescind this accessory cloth,” there is no fault. “After rescinding them, they must be determined again” is said with reference to one who wishes to use them after determining them by the name of a robe such as the outer robe, and so on. But for one who uses them after determining them only with the name “accessory cloth,” the previously made determination is itself the determination. “There is no act of determination”—by this, he shows that there is also no act of applying a kappabindu mark. The phrase “but the triple robe,” and so on, is stated with reference to what conforms to the measure of the triple robe, such as the “five-fistfuls,” and so on. “To determine the accessory cloth” means to make something into an accessory cloth and then determine it. Within a bounded sīmā, since there is the agreement for a sīmā of non-separation, there is no fault even in the case of robe-separation; thus, there is no difficulty of maintaining it there. He says, “In an unbounded sīmā, it is difficult to maintain.”

Anatirittappamāṇāti [M 2.0389] sugatavidatthiyā dīghaso cha vidatthiyo tiriyaṃ aḍḍhateyyavidatthiñca anatikkantappamāṇāti attho. Nanu ca vassikasāṭikā vassānātikkamena, kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi ābādhavūpasamena adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamenapi, kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi ābādhavūpasamenapi adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā “tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā”ti kasmā vuttaṃ. Sati hi adhiṭṭhāne paccuddhāro yuttoti? Ettha tāva tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu idaṃ vuttaṃ “paccuddharitvāti idaṃ paccuddharaṇaṃ sandhāya na vuttaṃ, paccuddharitvāti pana vassikasāṭikabhāvato apanetvāti evamattho gahetabbo. Tasmā hemantassa paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya [V 2.0344] antodasāhe vassikasāṭikabhāvato apanetvā vikappetabbāti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ ‘tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā’ti vutta”nti.

“Not exceeding the measure” means not surpassing the measure of six spans in length and two and a half spans in width, according to the Sugata's span. Now, is it not so that the rainy-season robe relinquishes its determination when the rainy season is over, and the itch-covering robe when the illness subsides? For this very reason, it is stated in the Mātikā Aṭṭhakathā: “The rainy-season robe relinquishes its determination when the months of the rains have passed, and the itch-covering robe when the illness subsides.” Therefore, why is it said, “After that, having rescinded it, it should be reassigned”? For when the determination is still in effect, is rescission proper? Here, regarding these three knotty points, this is stated: “'Having rescinded it'—this is not said in reference to that act of rescission, but rather, 'having rescinded it' means removing it from its status as a rainy-season robe. This is the meaning that should be understood. Therefore, to show the meaning that from the first day of winter onward, within ten days, it should be removed from its status as a rainy-season robe and reassigned, it is said, ‘After that, having rescinded it, it should be reassigned.’”

Keci pana “yathā kathinamāsabbhantare uppannacīvaraṃ kathinamāsātikkame nissaggiyaṃ hoti, evamayaṃ vassikasāṭikāpi vassānamāsātikkame nissaggiyā hoti, tasmā kattikapuṇṇamadivase paccuddharitvā tato paraṃ hemantassa paṭhamadivase vikappetabbāti evamattho gahetabbo. Paccuddharitvā tato paraṃ vikappetabbāti padayojanā veditabbā”ti ca vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Kathinamāse uppannañhi cīvaraṃ atirekacīvaraṭṭhāne ṭhitattā avasānadivase anadhiṭṭhitaṃ kathinamāsātikkame nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ pana vassikasāṭikā adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitattā na tena sadisāti vassānātikkame kathaṃ nissaggiyā hoti. Anadhiṭṭhitaavikappitameva hi taṃtaṃkālātikkame nissaggiyaṃ hoti, tasmā hemantepi vassikasāṭikā dasāhaṃ parihāraṃ labhatiyeva. Evaṃ kaṇḍuppaṭicchādipi ābādhavūpasamena adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, tasmā tato paraṃ dasāhaṃ parihāraṃ labhati, dasāhaṃ pana anatikkamitvā vikappetabbāti.

Some, however, say: “Just as a robe obtained within the Kathina month becomes liable to forfeiture if the Kathina month is exceeded, so too this rainy-season robe becomes liable to forfeiture if the rainy season months are exceeded. Therefore, it should be rescinded on the full moon day of Kattika, and then after that reassigned on the first day of winter—this is the meaning to be understood. The word-arrangement ‘Having rescinded it, it should be reassigned after that’ should be understood.” But this is not correct. For a robe obtained within the Kathina month, being in the state of an extra robe, becomes liable to forfeiture if the Kathina month is exceeded without being determined on the last day. But this rainy-season robe, having been determined and set aside, is not similar to that. Therefore, how could it become liable to forfeiture if the rainy season is exceeded? Indeed, only what is undetermined and unassigned becomes liable to forfeiture when its respective time is exceeded. Therefore, even in winter, the rainy-season robe certainly obtains a ten-day period of use. Similarly, the itch-covering robe also relinquishes its determination when the illness subsides. Therefore, after that, it obtains a ten-day period of use, but it must be reassigned without exceeding the ten days.

Keci pana “adhiṭṭhānabhedalakkhaṇe avuttattā vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamepi, kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi ābādhe vūpasantepi adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahati, tasmā ‘tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbā’ti idaṃ vutta”nti vadanti, taṃ mātikāṭṭhakathāya na sameti, samantapāsādikāya pana sameti. Tathā hi “vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamenapi, kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi [M 2.0390] ābādhavūpasamenapi adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatī”ti idaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ natthi, parivāraṭṭhakathāyañca “atthāpatti hemante āpajjati, no gimhe”ti ettha idaṃ vuttaṃ “kattikapuṇṇamāsiyā pacchime pāṭipadadivase vikappetvā ṭhapitaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ nivāsento hemante āpajjati. Kurundiyaṃ pana ‘kattikapuṇṇamadivase apaccuddharitvā hemante āpajjatī’ti vuttaṃ, tampi suvuttaṃ. Cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ, tato paraṃ vikappetunti hi vutta”nti (pari. aṭṭha. 323).

Some, however, say, “Because it is not stated in the characteristic of the breaking of determination, the rainy-season robe does not relinquish its determination even if the rainy season months are exceeded, and the itch-covering robe does not relinquish its determination even if the illness has subsided. Therefore, it is said, ‘After that, it should be rescinded and reassigned.’” This does not accord with the Mātikā Aṭṭhakathā, but it does accord with the Samantapāsādikā. For indeed, the statement “the rainy-season robe relinquishes its determination when the rainy season months have passed, and the itch-covering robe when the illness subsides” is not found in the Samantapāsādikā. Moreover, in the Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā, regarding “an offense is incurred in winter, not in summer,” this is stated: “If one wears a rainy-season robe that has been reassigned and kept on the day after the full-moon day of Kattika, one incurs an offense in winter. But in the Kurundī, it is said, ‘By not rescinding it on the full-moon day of Kattika, one incurs an offense in winter.’ That too is well said. For it is indeed said, ‘One should determine it for the four months, and thereafter, one should reassign it.’”

Tattha mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ nivāsanapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ vuttaṃ, kurundaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana apaccuddhārapaccayā. Tasmā kurundiyaṃ vuttanayeneva vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamepi adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatīti paññāyati. Kurundiyañhi “vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ, tato paraṃ vikappetu”nti vacanato yadi kattikapuṇṇamāyaṃ na paccuddhareyya, avijahitādhiṭṭhānā vassikasāṭikā hemantaṃ sampattā vikappanakkhette adhiṭṭhānasabbhāvato dukkaṭaṃ janeti, tasmā kattikapuṇṇamāyaṃ eva paccuddharitvā hemante vikappetabbāti iminā adhippāyena “kattikapuṇṇamadivase [V 2.0345] apaccuddharitvā hemante āpajjatī”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā vīmaṃsitvā yuttataraṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Therein, in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā, it is stated that a dukkaṭa offense arises on account of wearing it. In the Kurundaṭṭhakathā, however, it is on account of not withdrawing it. Therefore, by the method stated in the Kurundī, it is understood that the rains-cloth does not relinquish its determination even when the months of the rains have passed. For in the Kurundī, it is said, 'One should determine it for the four months of the rains, and thereafter, one should reassign it.' Accordingly, if one does not withdraw it on the full moon day of Kattika, the rains-cloth, with its determination unlapsed, having reached the winter season, generates a dukkaṭa offense because the determination exists in the sphere of reassignment. Therefore, with the intention that it should be withdrawn on the full moon day of Kattika itself and reassigned in the winter, it is said, 'Not having withdrawn it on the full moon day of Kattika, one incurs an offense in the winter.' Therefore, having investigated, the more appropriate view should be adopted.

Nahānatthāya anuññātattā “vaṇṇabhedamattarattāpi cesā vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Dve pana na vaṭṭantīti dvinnaṃ adhiṭṭhānābhāvato vuttaṃ. “Sace vassāne aparā vassikasāṭikā uppannā hoti, purimavassikasāṭikaṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetvā ca adhiṭṭhātabbā”ti vadanti. Pamāṇayuttanti dīghaso sugatavidatthiyā dve vidatthiyo, vitthārato diyaḍḍhā, dasā vidatthīti iminā pamāṇena yuttaṃ. Pamāṇikāti sugatavidatthiyā dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo, tiriyaṃ dve vidatthiyoti evaṃ vuttappamāṇayuttā. Paccuddharitvā vikappetabbāti ettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. “Sakiṃ adhiṭṭhitaṃ adhiṭṭhitameva hoti, puna na paccuddharīyati kālaparicchedābhāvato”ti vadanti. Apare pana “ekavacanenapi vaṭṭatīti dassanatthaṃ ‘sakiṃ adhiṭṭhitaṃ adhiṭṭhitamevā’ti vutta”nti vadanti. Ubhayatthāpi assa vacanassa idha vacane apubbaṃ payojanaṃ na dissati, teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ imasmiṃ ṭhāne “sakiṃ adhiṭṭhitaṃ adhiṭṭhitameva hotī”ti idaṃ padaṃ na vuttaṃ.

Because it is permitted for the purpose of bathing, it is said, 'Even if it is merely dyed a different color, it is allowed.' But it is said that two are not allowed because of the absence of determination for two. They say, 'If another rains-cloth arises during the rains, the previous rains-cloth should be determined after having been withdrawn and reassigned.' 'Proportionate in measure' means suitable by this measure: two spans in length by the Sugata's span and one and a half in width. 'Measured' means suitable by the stated measure: four spans in length by the Sugata's span and two spans across. Regarding 'it should be withdrawn and reassigned,' what is to be said here has already been stated below. Some say, 'Once determined, it remains determined; it is not withdrawn again because there is no time limit.' Others, however, say, 'To show that it is allowed even with a single utterance, it is said, "Once determined, it remains determined."' In both cases, no new purpose for this statement is seen in this context. Therefore, in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, this phrase 'once determined, it remains determined' is not stated in this place.

“Attano [M 2.0391] santakabhāvato mocetvā ṭhapitaṃ sandhāya mahāpaccariyaṃ anāpatti vuttā”ti vadanti. Iminā bhesajjaṃ cetāpessāmi, idaṃ mātuyā dassāmīti ṭhapentena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, idaṃ bhesajjassa, idaṃ mātuyāti vissajjetvā sakasantakabhāvato mocite adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthīti adhippāyo. Senāsanaparikkhāratthāya dinnapaccattharaṇeti ettha “anivāsetvā apārupitvā ca kevalaṃ mañcapīṭhesuyeva attharitvā paribhuñjiyamānaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ attano santakampi anadhiṭṭhātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Heṭṭhā pana “paccattharaṇampi adhiṭṭhātabbamevā”ti avisesena vuttattā attano santakaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbamevāti amhākaṃ khanti, vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ.

They say, 'In the Mahāpaccarī, it is stated that there is no offense concerning that which is set aside after being released from the state of being one's own property.' By this, the meaning is: when a monk sets something aside thinking, 'I will obtain medicine; I will give this to my mother,' it should be determined. But when it has been released from the state of being one's own property after having been relinquished with the thought, 'This is for medicine; this is for my mother,' there is no duty of determination. Here, regarding 'a spread given for the purpose of lodging requisites,' they say, 'A spread that is used by merely laying it out on beds and chairs, without wearing it or covering with it, is permissible not to determine, even if it is one's own property.' However, since it is stated below without distinction, 'Even a spread must indeed be determined,' it is our conviction that what is one's own property must indeed be determined. This should be adopted after investigation.

“Hīnāyāvattanenāti sikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya gihibhāvūpagamanenā”ti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ, taṃ yuttaṃ aññassa dāne viya cīvare nirālayabhāveneva pariccattattā. Keci pana “hīnāyāvattanenāti bhikkhuniyā gihibhāvūpagamanenā”ti evamatthaṃ gahetvā “bhikkhu pana vibbhamantopi yāva sikkhaṃ na paccakkhāti, tāva bhikkhuyevāti adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatī”ti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ “bhikkhuniyā hīnāyāvattanenā”ti visesetvā avuttattā. Bhikkhuniyā hi gihibhāvūpagamane adhiṭṭhānavijahanaṃ visuṃ vattabbaṃ natthi tassā vibbhamaneneva assamaṇībhāvato. Sikkhāpaccakkhānenāti pana idaṃ sace bhikkhuliṅge ṭhitova sikkhaṃ paccakkhāti[V 2.0346], tassa kāyalaggampi cīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Kaniṭṭhaṅgulinakhavasenāti heṭṭhimaparicchedaṃ dasseti. Pamāṇacīvarassāti pacchimappamāṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dve cīvarāni pārupantassāti antaragharappavesanatthāya suppaṭicchannasikkhāpade vuttanayena saṅghāṭiṃ uttarāsaṅgañca ekato katvā pārupantassa. Saṅgharitaṭṭhāneti dvīsupi antesu saṅgharitaṭṭhāne. Esa nayoti iminā pamāṇayuttesu yattha katthaci chiddaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, mahantesu pana tato parena chiddaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatīti ayamattho dassito. Sabbesūti ticīvarādibhedesu sabbacīvaresu.

'By reverting to a lower state' means by approaching the state of a householder without having renounced the training; this is stated in all three Gaṇṭhipadas. That is appropriate, because the robe has been relinquished simply by the state of having no attachment to it, just as in giving to another. Some, however, taking the meaning of 'by reverting to a lower state' as 'by a bhikkhunī approaching the state of a householder,' say, 'But a bhikkhu, even if he disrobes, as long as he does not renounce the training, he is still a bhikkhu; therefore, the determination is not relinquished.' That should not be accepted, because it is not stated with the specification 'by a bhikkhunī's reverting to a lower state.' For a bhikkhunī, the relinquishing of the determination upon approaching the state of a householder need not be stated separately, because by her very act of disrobing she ceases to be an ascetic. But this phrase 'by renouncing the training' is stated to show that if one, while still in the guise of a bhikkhu, renounces the training, even the robe attached to his body relinquishes its determination. 'By the measure of the little finger's nail' indicates the lower limit. 'Of a robe of standard size' is said referring to the final measure. 'For one wearing two robes' means for one who, for the purpose of entering a village, wears the saṅghāṭi and the uttarāsaṅga together, according to the method stated in the Suppaṭicchanna training rule. 'At the folded place' means at the folded place on both ends. By this, 'This is the principle,' this meaning is shown: in robes of standard size, a hole anywhere relinquishes the determination, but in large robes, a hole beyond that does not relinquish the determination. 'In all' means in all robes, with their divisions such as the three robes.

Aññaṃ pacchimappamāṇaṃ nāma natthīti sutte āgataṃ natthīti adhippāyo. Idāni tameva vibhāvetuṃ “yañhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Taṃ atikkamayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti vuttattā āha “tato uttari paṭisiddhattā”ti. Taṃ na sametīti parikkhāracoḷassa vikappanupagapacchimaṃ pacchimappamāṇanti gahetvā itaresaṃ ticīvarādīnaṃ muṭṭhipañcakādibhedaṃ pacchimappamāṇaṃ sandhāya “esa [M 2.0392] nayo”tiādivacanaṃ na sameti tādisassa pacchimappamāṇassa sutte abhāvatoti adhippāyo. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttavacanaṃ na sametīti imināva paṭikkhepena vikappanupagapacchimassa anto yattha katthaci chiddaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti ayampi nayo paṭikkhittoyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ticīvarañhi ṭhapetvā sesacīvaresu chiddena adhiṭṭhānavijahanaṃ nāma natthi, tasmā adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitesu sesacīvaresu vikappanupagapacchimaṃ appahontaṃ katvā khaṇḍākhaṇḍikaṃ chinnesupi adhiṭṭhānavijahanaṃ natthi. Sace pana adhiṭṭhānato pubbeyeva tādisaṃ hoti, acīvarattā adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthi. Khuddakaṃ cīvaranti muṭṭhipañcakādibhedappamāṇato anūnameva khuddakacīvaraṃ. Mahantaṃ vā khuddakaṃ karotīti ettha tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ catūsu passesu yasmiṃ padese chiddaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahati, tasmiṃ padese samantato chinditvā khuddakaṃ karontassa adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatīti adhippāyo.

The meaning is that there is nothing stated in the Sutta called 'another final limit.' Now, to clarify that very meaning, that which begins with 'yaṃ hi' and so on was stated. Because it was said, 'For one who exceeds that, there is a cutting pācittiya offense,' he said, 'because it is prohibited beyond that.' 'That does not fit' means: having taken the minimum robe suitable for formal sharing from among the requisite cloths as the 'final limit,' the statement beginning with 'this is the method,' which refers to the final limit of the other robes—such as the three robes, which is distinguished as five fist-widths—does not fit. The intention is that this is because such a final limit is not found in the Sutta. The statement made in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā does not fit. By this very refutation, it should be understood that this method—that a hole anywhere within the minimum robe suitable for formal sharing causes the determination to be abandoned—is also rejected. Indeed, excepting the three robes, there is no such thing as the abandoning of determination due to a hole in the remaining robes. Therefore, regarding the remaining robes that have been set aside after being determined, even if they are cut into pieces, making them insufficient for the minimum size suitable for formal sharing, there is no abandoning of the determination. But if it is in such a state even before the determination, because it is not a valid robe, there is no function of determination. 'A small robe' is a small robe that is not less than the measure distinguished as five fist-widths, and so on. In the phrase 'or makes a large one small,' the intention is this: with regard to the three robes, in whichever place on the four sides a hole does not cause the determination to be abandoned, for one who makes it small by cutting all around that place, the determination is not abandoned.

Sammukhāvikappanā parammukhāvikappanāti ettha sammukhena vikappanā parammukhena vikappanāti evamattho gahetabbo. Sannihitāsannihitabhāvanti āsannadūrabhāvaṃ. Āsannadūrabhāvo ca adhiṭṭhāne vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Paribhogādayopi vaṭṭantīti ettha adhiṭṭhānassapi antogadhattā sace saṅghāṭiādināmena adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjitukāmo hoti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ kātabbaṃ. No ce, na kātabbaṃ, vikappanameva pamāṇaṃ, tasmā atirekacīvaraṃ nāma na hoti. Mittoti daḷhamitto. Sandiṭṭhoti diṭṭhamitto nātidaḷhamitto. Vikappitavikappanā nāmesā vaṭṭatīti adhiṭṭhitaadhiṭṭhānaṃ viyāti adhippāyo avisesena vuttavacananti ticīvarādiṃ adhiṭṭheti, vassikasāṭikaṃ kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiñca [V 2.0347] vikappetīti avatvā sabbacīvarānaṃ avisesena vikappetīti vuttavacanaṃ. Ticīvarasaṅkhepenāti ticīvaranīhārena, saṅghāṭiādiadhiṭṭhānavasenāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Here, in 'face-to-face formal sharing and out-of-sight formal sharing,' the meaning should be understood thus: 'formal sharing in one's presence' and 'formal sharing in one's absence.' 'The state of being present and not present' means the state of being near and far. And the state of being near and far should be understood by the very method stated in the section on determination. Here, in 'use and so on are also allowable,' because determination is also included, if one wishes to use a robe after determining it by a name such as 'outer robe,' the determination should be made. If not, it should not be done; formal sharing itself is the standard. Therefore, there is no such thing as an extra robe. 'A friend' means a firm friend. 'An acquaintance' means a friend one has seen, not a very firm friend. 'This, called "formally sharing what has been formally shared," is allowable'—the intention is that it is like determining what has already been determined. 'A statement made without distinction' is the statement that says one formally shares all robes without distinction, instead of saying, 'One determines the three robes, etc., and one formally shares the rains-bathing cloth and the itch-covering cloth.' 'By way of the three robes' means by the method of the three robes; that is to say, by way of determining the outer robe, and so on.

Tuyhaṃ demītiādīsu “tasmiṃ kāle na gaṇhitukāmopi sace na paṭikkhipati, puna gaṇhitukāmatāya sati gahetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti. Itthannāmassāti parammukhe ṭhitaṃ sandhāya vadati. “Tuyhaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti vutte “mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti vadati, sudinnaṃ suggahitañcāti ettha “yathā parato ‘tava santakaṃ karohī’ti vutte duddinnampi ‘sādhu, bhante, mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī’ti vacanena ‘suggahitaṃ hotī’ti vuttaṃ, evamidhāpi ‘tuyhaṃ gaṇhāhī’ti vutte sudinnattā [M 2.0393] ‘mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī’ti avuttepi ‘sudinnamevā’”ti vadanti. “Gaṇhāhīti ca āṇattiyā gahaṇassa tappaṭibaddhatākaraṇavasena pavattattā tadā gaṇhāmīti citte anuppādite pacchā gahetuṃ na labhatī”ti vadanti.

In cases such as 'I give to you,' they say: 'Even if one does not wish to accept at that time, if one does not refuse, it is allowable to accept later when the wish to accept arises.' 'It belongs to so-and-so'—this is said in reference to someone who is absent. When 'Take it for yourself' is said, one says, 'I take it for myself.' Here, regarding 'well-given and well-received,' they say: 'Just as it is said elsewhere that when "Make it your own" is said, even if it was poorly given, by the words "Very well, venerable sir, I take it for myself," it becomes "well-received"; so too here, when "Take it for yourself" is said, because it is well-given, even if "I take it for myself" is not said, it is still "well-given."' And they say: 'Since "Take it" proceeds by way of making the act of taking dependent on the command, if the thought "I am taking it" is not produced in the mind at that time, one does not get to take it later.'

Taṃ na yujjatīti vinayakammassa karaṇavasena gahetvā dinnattā vuttaṃ. Sace pana paro saccatoyeva vissāsaṃ gaṇhāti, puna kenaci kāraṇena tena dinnaṃ tassa na vaṭṭatīti natthi. Nissaggiyaṃ pana cīvaraṃ jānitvā vā ajānitvā vā gaṇhantaṃ “mā gaṇhāhī”ti nivāraṇatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Kāyavācāhi kattabbaadhiṭṭhānavikappanānaṃ akatattā hotīti āha “kāyavācāto samuṭṭhātī”ti. Cīvarassa attano santakatā, jātippamāṇayuttatā, chinnapalibodhabhāvo, atirekacīvaratā, dasāhātikkamoti imānettha pañca aṅgāni.

'That is not correct'—this was said because it was given after being taken by way of performing a formal act of the Vinaya. But if the other person truly accepts it with trust, there is no case where, for some reason, what was given by the former would be unallowable for the latter. But regarding a robe that is to be forfeited, the statement 'Do not take it' was said for the purpose of preventing one from taking it, whether knowing or not knowing. Because the determination and formal sharing that should be done by body and speech have not been done, it occurs; therefore, he said, 'It arises from body and speech.' Here, these are the five factors: the robe being one's own property; its being of the right kind and measure; the state of being free from obstruction; its being an extra robe; and the passing of ten days.

Paṭhamakathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the first training rule concerning the Kathina is concluded.

2. Udositasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Udosita Training Rule

471-473. Dutiye athānandatthero kathaṃ okāsaṃ paṭilabhati, kiṃ karonto ca āhiṇḍatīti āha “thero kirā”tiādi. Avippavāseti nimittatthe bhummaṃ, avippavāsatthanti attho, vippavāsapaccayā yā āpatti, tadabhāvatthanti vuttaṃ hoti.

In the second case: How does the Elder Ānanda obtain an opportunity, and what is he doing while wandering? In response, it is said, “The Elder, indeed…” and so on. Regarding ‘avippavāseti’, the locative case is used in the sense of ‘nimitta’ (purpose); the meaning is ‘for the purpose of non-separation’. It is said that this is for the purpose of the absence of whatever offense arises from the condition of separation.

475-476. Evaṃ chinnapalibodhoti evaṃ imehi cīvaraniṭṭhānakathinubbhārehi chinnapalibodho. Adhiṭṭhitesūti ticīvarādhiṭṭhānanayena adhiṭṭhitesu. Ticīvarena vippavuttho hotīti “rukkho chinno, paṭo daḍḍho”tiādīsu viya avayavepi samudāyavohāro labbhatīti vuttaṃ.

Thus, ‘the obstacles are cut off’ means that the obstacles are cut off by these matters of robe-completion and Kathina-withdrawal. Regarding ‘adhiṭṭhitesu’ (when determined), it means when determined according to the method of determining the three robes. Regarding ‘ticīvarena vippavuttho hoti’ (he is separated from the three robes), it is said that a collective term is applicable even to a part, just as in expressions like ‘the tree is cut’ or ‘the cloth is burned,’ and so on.

477-478. Parikhāya [V 2.0348] vā parikkhittoti iminā ca samantā nadītaḷākādiudakena parikkhittopi parikkhittoyevāti dasseti. Ettāvatāti “parikkhitto”ti iminā vacanena. Ākāse aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetīti gharassa upari ākāse aḍḍhateyyaratanappamāṇaṃ atikkamitvā aruṇaṃ [M 2.0394] uṭṭhāpeti. Gharaṃ nivesanudositādilakkhaṇameva, na pana pāṭiyekkaṃ gharaṃ nāma atthīti āha “ettha cā”tiādi.

Regarding ‘parikhāya vā parikkhitto’ (or surrounded by a moat), by this it is shown that even if surrounded on all sides by water from a river, lake, or the like, it is indeed considered surrounded. Regarding ‘ettāvatā’ (by this much), it means by this word ‘parikkhitto’ (surrounded). Regarding ‘ākāse aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpeti’ (he raises the dawn in the sky), it means he raises the dawn in the sky above the house, having exceeded a measure of two and a half ratanas. A house is merely characterized as a dwelling, an abode, or the like; there is no separate thing called a ‘house.’ Thus, he said, ‘ettha cā’ (here too), and so on.

479. Pāḷiyaṃ vuttanayena “sabhāye”ti avatvā “sabhāya”nti paccattavacanaṃ sabhāya-saddassa napuṃsakaliṅgatāvibhāvanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Sabhā-saddapariyāyopi hi sabhāya-saddo napuṃsakaliṅgayutto idha vuttoti imamatthaṃ dassento “liṅgabyattayena sabhā vuttā”ti āha. Cīvarahatthapāse vasitabbaṃ natthīti cīvarahatthapāseyeva vasitabbanti natthi. Yaṃ tassā…pe… na vijahitabbanti ettha tassā vīthiyā sammukhaṭṭhāne sabhāyadvārānaṃ gahaṇeneva tattha sabbānipi gehāni sā ca antaravīthi gahitāyeva hoti. Atiharitvā ghare nikkhipatīti taṃ vīthiṃ muñcitvā ṭhite aññasmiṃ ghare nikkhipati. Purato vā pacchato vā hatthapāseti gharassa hatthapāsaṃ sandhāya vadati.

479. In the Pāḷi, instead of saying ‘sabhāye’ in the stated manner, the nominative singular ‘sabhāyaṃ’ is used to make clear the neuter gender of the word ‘sabhāya’. To show the meaning that here the word ‘sabhāya’, a synonym for the word ‘sabhā’, is used in the neuter gender, he said: ‘Sabhā is stated with a change of gender.’ The statement ‘cīvarahatthapāse vasitabbaṃ’ (one must dwell within hand's reach of the robe) does not exist; the meaning is that it is not the case that one must dwell only within hand's reach of the robe. Regarding ‘yaṃ tassā…pe… na vijahitabbaṃ’ (that… should not be abandoned), here, by the very inclusion of the doors of the assembly hall in a place facing that street, all the houses there and that inner street are indeed included. Regarding ‘atiharitvā ghare nikkhipati’ (having carried it beyond, he places it in a house), it means having left that street, he places it in another house situated elsewhere. Regarding ‘purato vā pacchato vā hatthapāse’ (within hand's reach in front or behind), he speaks with reference to the hand's reach of the house.

Nivesanādīsu parikkhittatāya ekūpacāratā, aparikkhittatāya nānūpacāratā ca veditabbāti dassento “etenevupāyenā”tiādimāha. Nivesanādīni gāmato bahi sanniviṭṭhāni gahitānīti veditabbaṃ. Antogāme ṭhitānañhi gāmaggahaṇena gahitattā gāmaparihāroyevāti. Sabbatthāpīti gāmādīsu ajjhokāsapariyantesu pannarasasu. Parikkhepādivasenāti ettha ādi-saddena aparikkhepasseva gahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ, na ekakulādīnampi.

To show that in dwellings and so on, due to being enclosed there is a single precinct, and due to being unenclosed there are multiple precincts, he said, ‘By this very method,’ and so on. It should be understood that dwellings and so on that are situated outside a village are included. For those situated inside a village, because they are included by the inclusion of ‘village’, it is simply the village boundary. Regarding ‘sabbatthāpi’ (in all cases), it means in the fifteen places beginning with a village and ending with open space. Regarding ‘parikkhepādivasena’ (by way of enclosure, etc.), here, by the word ‘ādi’ (etc.), the inclusion of only the unenclosed should be understood, and not also of ‘one family’, etc.

480-487. Ovarako nāma gabbhassa abbhantare añño gabbhotipi vadanti. Muṇḍacchadanapāsādoti candikaṅgaṇayutto pāsādo.
