Sannihitabalavabhayānīti corehi manussānaṃ hataviluttākoṭitabhāvadassanato [M 2.0447] sannihitabalavabhayānīti attho. Sace pacchimikāyātiādinā vuttamevatthaṃ byatirekamukhena vibhāveti. Yatra hi piṇḍāyātiādinā vuttappamāṇameva visesetvā dasseti. Sāsaṅkasappaṭibhayamevāti ettha sāsaṅkaṃ vā sappaṭibhayaṃ vā hotu, vaṭṭatiyeva.

'Deemed dangerous' (sāsaṅkāni) means they are considered 'dangerous' by seeing the places, and so on, where thieves have settled. 'With imminent and strong fear' (sannihitabalavabhayāni) means that because one sees the state of people being killed, plundered, and beaten by thieves, there is imminent and strong fear; this is the meaning. By 'If to the western direction,' and so on, it clarifies the very meaning already stated by way of contrast. By 'Where for alms-food,' and so on, it shows the very measure already stated by specifying it. Herein, regarding 'dangerous and fraught with fear indeed' (sāsaṅkaṃ sappaṭibhayameva), whether it be dangerous or fraught with fear, it is indeed allowable.

Pāḷiyaṃ “siyā ca tassa bhikkhuno kocideva paccayo tena cīvarena vippavāsāya, chārattaparamaṃ tena bhikkhunā tena cīvarena vippavasitabba”nti iminā antaraghare cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā tasmiṃ vihāre vasantassa aññattha gamanakicce sati vihārato bahi chārattaṃ vippavāso anuññāto. Vasanaṭṭhānato hi aññattha chārattaṃ vippavāso vutto, na tasmiṃ vihāre vasantassa. Tena ca “puna gāmasīmaṃ okkamitvāti ettha sace gocaragāmato puratthimāya disāya senāsanaṃ, ayañca pacchimadisaṃ gato hotī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatoyeva ca mātikāṭṭhakathāyampi (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. sāsaṅkasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “tato ce uttari vippavaseyyā”ti [V 2.0396] ettha “chārattato uttari tasmiṃ senāsane sattamaṃ aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpeyyā”ti attho vutto. Bhadantabuddhadattācariyena pana pākaṭataraṃ katvā ayamevattho vutto. Vuttañhi tena –

In the Pāḷi, by this passage: 'If that bhikkhu has some reason for separation from that robe, that bhikkhu may be separated from that robe for a maximum of six nights,' it is permitted for a bhikkhu who, having placed a robe within a house, is dwelling in that monastery, if there is a need to go elsewhere, to be separated from the robe for six nights outside the monastery. For separation for six nights is stated with reference to being elsewhere from the dwelling place, not for one who is dwelling in that monastery. And by that it is stated, 'If, after re-entering the village boundary... in this context, if the lodging is in the eastern direction from the alms-resort village, and this one has gone to the western direction,' and so forth. And for that very reason, also in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, in reference to the phrase 'if he should be separated beyond that,' the meaning is stated as: 'beyond six nights, he should not cause the seventh dawn to arise in that lodging.' However, the venerable teacher Bhadantabuddhadatta, having made it more clear, stated this very meaning. For it was stated by him:

“Yaṃ gāmaṃ gocaraṃ katvā, bhikkhu āraññake vase;

Tasmiṃ gāme ṭhapetuṃ taṃ, māsamekantu vaṭṭati.

Having made a certain village his alms resort, a bhikkhu dwells in the forest; it is allowable for him to place it in that village for one whole month.

“Aññattheva vasantassa, chārattaparamaṃ mataṃ;

Ayamassa adhippāyo, paṭicchanno pakāsito”ti.

For one dwelling elsewhere indeed, a maximum of six nights is to be known; this hidden intention of this rule has been revealed.

“Kosambiyaṃ aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hotī”ti āgatattā “kosambakasammuti anuññātā”ti vuttaṃ. Kosambakassa bhikkhuno sammuti kosambakasammuti. Senāsanaṃ āgantvāti vusitavihārasseva sandhāya vuttattā tasmiṃ gāmūpacārepi aññasmiṃ vihāre aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Vasitvāti aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetvā. Gataṭṭhānassa atidūrattā “evaṃ asakkontenā”ti vuttaṃ. Tatthevāti tasmiṃyeva gataṭṭhāne.

Because it has come in the text thus: 'In Kosambī a certain bhikkhu was ill,' it is stated, 'the Kosambaka designation was permitted.' The designation for the bhikkhu of Kosambī is the Kosambaka designation. As for 'having come to the lodging,' since this is stated with reference to the very monastery one has dwelt in, it is not allowable to cause the dawn to arise in another monastery, even in that village-access. 'Having dwelt' means having caused the dawn to arise. Because the place one has gone to is too far, it was stated, 'by one unable to return thus.' 'There itself' means in that very place one has gone to.

Sāsaṅkasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on what is fraught with danger is concluded.

10. Pariṇatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Dedicated Offerings

657-659. Dasame [M 2.0448] uddissa ṭhapitabhāgeti attano gharepi uddisitvā visuṃ ṭhapitakoṭṭhāse. “Ekaṃ mayhaṃ, ekaṃ imassa dehī”ti evaṃ ekavācāya āpajjitabbattā “āpajjeyya ekato”ti vuttaṃ. Tumhākaṃ sappiādīni ābhatānīti tumhākaṃ atthāya ābhatāni sappiādīni. Pariṇatabhāvaṃ jānitvāpi vuttavidhinā viññāpentena tesaṃ santakameva viññāpitaṃ nāma hotīti āha – “mayhampi dethāti vadati, vaṭṭatī”ti.

In the tenth rule, 'in the portion set aside having designated' means: in the portion set aside separately, having designated it, even in one's own house. Because the offense is to be incurred by a single utterance, such as, 'Give one to me, and one to this person,' it is stated, 'one would incur the offense at once.' 'Ghee and so on brought for you' means ghee and so on brought for your sake. Even knowing that it has been dedicated, for one who requests according to the stated method, it is considered a request for what is indeed the donors' own property. Thus it is said: 'He says, "Give to me also," and it is allowable.'

660. Pupphampi āropetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti idaṃ pariṇataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace pana ekasmiṃ cetiye pūjitaṃ pupphaṃ gahetvā aññasmiṃ cetiye pūjeti, vaṭṭati. Ṭhitaṃ disvāti sesakaṃ gahetvā ṭhitaṃ disvā. Imassa sunakhassa mā dehi, etassa dehīti idaṃ pariṇateyeva. Tiracchānagatassa pariccajitvā dinne pana taṃ palāpetvā aññaṃ bhuñjāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. “Kattha demātiādinā ekenākārena pāḷiyaṃ anāpatti dassitā, evaṃ pana apucchitepi apariṇataṃ idanti [V 2.0397] jānantena attano ruciyā yattha icchati, tattha dāpetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Yattha icchatha, tattha dethāti etthāpi “tumhākaṃ ruciyā”ti vuttattā yattha icchati, tattha dāpetuṃ labhati. Pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayenevāti “yattha tumhākaṃ deyyadhammo”tiādinā nayena. Saṅghapariṇatabhāvo, taṃ ñatvā attano pariṇāmanaṃ, paṭilābhoti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.

660. The statement 'It is not allowable to offer even a flower' is said with reference to what has been dedicated. However, if one takes a flower offered at one shrine and offers it at another shrine, it is permissible. 'Having seen it placed' means having seen the remainder that was taken and placed. 'Do not give to this dog, give to that one'—this refers only to what has been dedicated. But when something has been given to an animal after having been relinquished, it is allowable to drive that one away and cause another to eat. By one method, such as 'Where shall we give?', non-offense is shown in the Pāḷi. However, even when not asked thus, one who knows 'this is not dedicated' may, according to one's own preference, cause it to be given wherever one wishes—this is stated in all three sub-commentaries. Also in the case of 'Give wherever you wish,' since it is said 'according to your preference,' one may cause it to be given wherever one wishes. 'By the very method that has come in the Pāḷi' means by the method such as 'wherever your offering is...' The three factors here are: the state of being dedicated to the Saṅgha; knowing that, the diverting of it to oneself; and the receiving.

Pariṇatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on dedicated offerings is concluded.

Niṭṭhito pattavaggo tatiyo.

The third chapter, the Bowl Chapter, is concluded.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya sāratthadīpaniyaṃ

Thus, in the Sāratthadīpanī, the Subcommentary on the Vinaya Commentary Samantapāsādikā—

Nissaggiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Forfeiture Rules is concluded.

Dutiyo bhāgo niṭṭhito.

The second volume is concluded.
